PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: prop-blue-torches
Workflow profile: 2X3_VERTICAL (2:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Prop/artifact guard: transfer only material response, patina, highlight rolloff, and photographic presentation. Do not add a glowing sword, sacred symbols, blood, or human hands unless this row explicitly requires them.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
BLUE-FLAME FORTRESS TORCHES — PRODUCTION REFERENCE: HERO PROP DESIGN, CONSTRUCTION, MATERIALS, SCALE, AND CONTINUITY.

Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Isolated production-reference hero prop of Hell's fortress blue-flame wall torch from JESUS: THE HARROWING OF HELL, shown as a complete physical object in its pre-transformation initial hell-realm state. The fixture is an ancient wall-mounted torch sconce forged for the cathedral of suffering at Hell's Gate: a vertical iron shaft roughly forearm-length, thick as a man's wrist, hammered from blackened wrought iron with deep pitting, scale, and centuries of corrosion. The upper cup is a flared iron bowl ringed with short, jagged prongs that grip a dense mass of charred resinous fuel and blackened linen-wrapped pitch, still intact and smoking. Around the shaft, irregular bands of corroded bronze and fused bone fragments have been riveted or heat-welded into the iron—ribs of pale yellowed bone, knuckle-like joints, and thin cranial shards partially melted into the metal so the torch itself feels grown from the same iron-and-bone language as Hell's Gate. A heavy L-shaped wall bracket of the same black iron extends from the shaft, ending in a broad mounting plate with crude square-headed rivets and dried blood-dark residue in the crevices; the plate is sized for anchoring into obsidian-black fortress stone. Optional short iron chain links hang from a side ring, lightly swinging, oxidized and soot-blackened.

The flame is the defining supernatural element: cold blue fire, royal-blue to sapphire core (#4169E1) with sharper cyan-white inner tongues and deeper indigo outer edges, never ordinary orange campfire yellow. The flame burns steadily but with an unnatural, slow-lapping motion, as if the fire itself is older and colder than earthly combustion. Subtle translucent blue smoke and fine ash particles rise from the fuel mass. The flame casts cold accent light onto the iron and bone, rimming edges with electric blue specular highlights while leaving deep crimson-black shadows in recessed corrosion pits—matching fortress lighting of cold blue torch illumination against red underglow. No golden divine fire yet; this is strictly the hell-realm blue state before the chamber transforms black stone to white marble and blue flame to golden fire.

Materials read tactile and photoreal: rough hammer marks on iron, powdery black scale flaking at edges, greasy soot film on the upper bowl, matte bone with micro-cracks and darkened marrow channels, verdigris and rust blooms where bronze meets iron, residual dried blood-brown stains on rivets and bone seams. Scale is human-handable wall torch, not a giant braziers—one complete sconce fully visible, roughly 18–24 inches tall excluding flame, flame extending another 8–12 inches above the cup. Slight heat shimmer above the blue tips. Atmosphere: thin wisps of hell smoke and ash floating past, not obscuring the object.

Lighting for the prop study: soft dark studio void of obsidian black (#0A0A0A) with a faint deep crimson fill from below (~3500K red underglow) so the iron silhouette stays readable, and the blue flame as practical key light painting cold highlights on metal and bone. Photoreal live-action biblical epic production reference, sacred-serious tone, not fantasy cartoon, not neon sci-fi plasma. Camera: 85mm close product framing, slight three-quarter angle showing shaft, cup, flame, bracket, and bone inlays together, shallow depth of field with the flame and upper cup tack-sharp and the lower mounting plate softly falling off. Color grade locked to hell initial palette: deep crimsons, obsidian blacks, cold blue accents. Continuity locks: blue flame only (never gold on this asset); iron-and-bone material language consistent with Hell's Gate; wall-sconce form usable as set dressing on fortress pillars and gate walls; no modern fittings, gas valves, glass, plastic, wiring, or electric bulbs. No readable inscriptions, sigils-as-text, logos, captions, watermarks, or borders on the object or frame. Single complete torch object, physically coherent materials, accurate scale for human hands and fortress walls. Neutral production reference framing, the complete object visible, accurate materials and scale, no labels or text.
